questions.question: Neither Rahul nor his friends ______ present.
questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('friends' -> 'were').

questions.question: Either the teacher or the students ______ responsible.
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('students' -> 'are').

questions.question: Bread and butter ______ his daily breakfast.
questions.explanation: When two singular nouns together express a single idea/dish, they take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: The Minister, as well as his secretaries, ______ arrived.
questions.explanation: When two nouns are connected by 'as well as', 'along with', or 'together with', the verb agrees with the first subject ('The Minister' -> 'has').

questions.question: The captain, along with the players, ______ given a warm welcome.
questions.explanation: Subjects joined by 'along with' take a verb agreeing with the first subject ('captain' -> 'was').

questions.question: Each of the boys ______ given a prize.
questions.explanation: 'Each of' + plural noun takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Neither of the two candidates ______ suitable for the job.
questions.explanation: 'Neither of' refers to none of the two individually, taking a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: One of my friends ______ a doctor.
questions.explanation: 'One of' + plural noun takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: He is one of the players who ______ selected for the team.
questions.explanation: In 'one of the [plural noun] who/which/that', the relative pronoun refers to the plural antecedent ('players'), taking plural verb ('have been').

questions.question: This is the only one of his novels that ______ interesting.
questions.explanation: When 'the only one of' is used, the relative pronoun refers to 'the only one' (singular), taking a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: More than one person ______ involved in the scam.
questions.explanation: 'More than one' followed by a singular countable noun takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: More students than one ______ absent today.
questions.explanation: 'More [plural noun] than one' takes a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: A number of students ______ participating in the event.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' takes a plural verb ('are'), whereas 'The number of' takes a singular verb.

questions.question: The number of accidents ______ increasing day by day.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' expresses a specific statistical figure, taking a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Ten miles ______ a long distance to walk.
questions.explanation: A plural unit of measurement/distance considered as a single quantity takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Fifty thousand rupees ______ a large amount.
questions.explanation: A specific sum of money viewed as a whole takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Mathematics ______ an interesting subject.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects/disciplines ending in '-s' (Mathematics, Physics, Civics) take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: His mathematics ______ very weak.
questions.explanation: When 'mathematics' refers to calculation skills/arithmetic, it takes a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: The news ______ true.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and always takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: The jury ______ divided in their opinion.
questions.explanation: When members of a collective noun (jury, committee) act individually or hold differing opinions, it takes a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: The jury ______ given its verdict.
questions.explanation: When a collective noun acts as a unified single body (indicated by pronoun 'its'), it takes a singular verb ('has').

questions.question: The committee ______ unanimous on this issue.
questions.explanation: 'Unanimous' indicates complete unity of the collective body, taking a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: The police ______ investigating the robbery.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun in English, requiring a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Cattle ______ grazing in the meadow.
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is always plural without an '-s', requiring a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Poultry ______ sold here.
questions.explanation: 'Poultry' is a collective plural noun taking a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Gulliver's Travels ______ written by Jonathan Swift.
questions.explanation: The title of a book/novel takes a singular verb even if it ends in '-s' ('was').

questions.question: The Arabian Nights ______ an evergreen collection of stories.
questions.explanation: Book titles take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: The United States ______ a powerful nation.
questions.explanation: The name of a country takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Every man, woman, and child ______ rescued.
questions.explanation: Singular nouns preceded by 'every' take a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Many a soldier ______ lost in the battle.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' is followed by a singular countable noun and takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: A good deal of time ______ wasted.
questions.explanation: 'A good deal of' with uncountable noun ('time') takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: A lot of work ______ still pending.
questions.explanation: 'A lot of' with uncountable noun ('work') takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: A lot of books ______ donated to the library.
questions.explanation: 'A lot of' with countable plural noun ('books') takes a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: None of the information ______ accurate.
questions.explanation: 'None of' + uncountable noun takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: None of the players ______ ready.
questions.explanation: 'None of' + plural countable noun takes a plural verb in standard PSC usage ('were').

questions.question: The quality of these mangoes ______ not good.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun 'The quality' (not 'mangoes'), so it takes 'is'.

questions.question: The cost of essential commodities ______ gone up.
questions.explanation: The true subject is singular 'The cost', taking 'has'.

questions.question: Slow and steady ______ the race.
questions.explanation: Proverbial pair representing a single concept takes a singular verb ('wins').

questions.question: Time and tide ______ for no man.
questions.explanation: In standard English and Kerala PSC convention, 'Time and tide' takes plural verb 'wait'.

questions.question: No news ______ good news.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable singular, taking 'is'.

questions.question: The scissors ______ sharp.
questions.explanation: Tools/clothing with two parts (scissors, trousers, spectacles) take a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: A pair of scissors ______ kept on the table.
questions.explanation: When preceded by 'A pair of', the subject is singular ('A pair'), taking 'is'.

questions.question: My spectacles ______ missing.
questions.explanation: 'Spectacles' takes a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: A pair of shoes ______ bought yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'A pair of shoes' takes singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Two and two ______ four.
questions.explanation: Mathematical facts can take singular 'makes' or 'is' in PSC questions.

questions.question: Physics ______ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Academic discipline ending in '-s' takes singular 'is'.

questions.question: The clergy ______ invited to the ceremony.
questions.explanation: 'Clergy' is a group noun treated as plural ('were').

questions.question: The poor ______ suffering during the flood.
questions.explanation: 'The + adjective' (The poor, the rich) refers to the entire class of people and takes a plural verb ('are').

questions.question: The rich ______ not always happy.
questions.explanation: 'The rich' represents all wealthy people, taking plural 'are'.

questions.question: The blind ______ guided safely.
questions.explanation: 'The blind' refers to blind people collectively, taking plural verb 'were'.

questions.question: Neither praise nor blame ______ to affect him.
questions.explanation: When subjects joined by 'neither...nor' are both singular ('praise', 'blame'), the verb is singular ('seems').

questions.question: Either you or he ______ mistaken.
questions.explanation: With 'either...or', verb agrees with nearer subject ('he' -> 'is').

questions.question: Neither he nor I ______ guilty.
questions.explanation: Nearer subject to verb is 'I', taking 'am'.

questions.question: He and I ______ good friends.
questions.explanation: Two pronouns joined by 'and' form a plural compound subject, taking 'are'.

questions.question: Fire and water ______ not agree.
questions.explanation: Two distinct elements joined by 'and' take plural verb 'do'.

questions.question: Gold and silver ______ precious metals.
questions.explanation: Two distinct subjects joined by 'and' take plural 'are'.

questions.question: The poet and philosopher ______ dead.
questions.explanation: When one article ('The') precedes the first noun only, both nouns refer to the same person, taking singular 'is'.

questions.question: The poet and the philosopher ______ dead.
questions.explanation: When articles precede both nouns ('The poet and the philosopher'), two distinct persons are meant, taking plural 'are'.

questions.question: The collector and district magistrate ______ on leave.
questions.explanation: Single article 'The' indicates one person holding both offices, taking singular 'is'.

questions.question: A black and white cow ______ grazing in the field.
questions.explanation: Single article 'A' indicates one cow with two colors, taking singular 'is'.

questions.question: A black and a white cow ______ grazing.
questions.explanation: Two articles ('A black and a white cow') indicate two separate cows, taking plural 'are'.

questions.question: Not only the principal but also the teachers ______ present.
questions.explanation: 'Not only...but also' agrees with the nearer subject ('teachers' -> 'were').

questions.question: Not only the students but also the teacher ______ present.
questions.explanation: 'Not only...but also' agrees with the nearer subject ('teacher' -> 'was').

questions.question: Drinking and driving ______ a punishable offence.
questions.explanation: Compound gerund phrase viewed as a single act takes singular 'is'.

questions.question: Early to bed and early to rise ______ a man healthy.
questions.explanation: Compound habit treated as a single lifestyle concept takes singular verb 'makes'.

questions.question: The majority of students ______ passed the exam.
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' + plural noun takes a plural verb ('have').

questions.question: The majority ______ in favor of the proposal.
questions.explanation: When 'the majority' is used alone as a single voting block, it takes singular verb 'was'.

questions.question: Two-thirds of the book ______ interesting.
questions.explanation: Fractions of a singular entity ('the book') take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Two-thirds of the books ______ sold.
questions.explanation: Fractions of plural countable entities ('the books') take a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: Half of the milk ______ spoiled.
questions.explanation: 'Half of' + uncountable noun ('milk') takes singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Half of the students ______ absent.
questions.explanation: 'Half of' + plural noun takes plural verb ('were').

questions.question: Everyone ______ ready to participate.
questions.explanation: Indefinite pronoun 'Everyone' always takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Somebody ______ left their umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'Somebody' takes a singular verb ('has').

questions.question: Anybody ______ welcome to join.
questions.explanation: 'Anybody' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Nobody ______ perfect.
questions.explanation: 'Nobody' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Everything ______ in its place.
questions.explanation: 'Everything' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Something ______ burning in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: 'Something' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Nothing ______ impossible for a willing heart.
questions.explanation: 'Nothing' takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Each boy and each girl ______ given a certificate.
questions.explanation: Nouns qualified by 'each' take a singular verb ('was') even when joined by 'and'.

questions.question: Every student and every teacher ______ present.
questions.explanation: Nouns qualified by 'every' take a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: No boy and no girl ______ absent.
questions.explanation: Singular nouns joined by 'and' and qualified by 'no' take a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: The Prime Minister, accompanied by his ministers, ______ arriving today.
questions.explanation: 'Accompanied by' follows the first subject ('The Prime Minister' -> 'is').

questions.question: The ship, with its crew, ______ lost at sea.
questions.explanation: 'with' follows the primary subject ('The ship' -> 'was').

questions.question: Ravi, together with his cousins, ______ going to the park.
questions.explanation: 'together with' takes the verb according to the first subject ('Ravi' -> 'is').

questions.question: Honesty, as well as diligence, ______ rewarded.
questions.explanation: 'as well as' agrees with the first subject ('Honesty' -> 'is').

questions.question: The house, in addition to the furniture, ______ insured.
questions.explanation: 'in addition to' agrees with the main subject ('The house' -> 'is').

questions.question: All that glitters ______ not gold.
questions.explanation: Proverbial idiom 'All that glitters' takes singular 'is'.

questions.question: All the money ______ spent.
questions.explanation: 'All' referring to an uncountable quantity ('money') takes singular 'was'.

questions.question: All the passengers ______ safe.
questions.explanation: 'All' referring to countable plural entities ('passengers') takes plural 'were'.

questions.question: Some of the pie ______ eaten.
questions.explanation: 'Some of' + singular noun takes singular verb 'was'.

questions.question: Some of the pies ______ eaten.
questions.explanation: 'Some of' + plural noun takes plural verb 'were'.

questions.question: Measles ______ an infectious disease.
questions.explanation: Names of diseases ending in '-s' (Measles, Mumps, Rickets) take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Billiards ______ played by two players.
questions.explanation: Names of games ending in '-s' (Billiards, Darts, Dominoes) take a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Darts ______ a popular pub game in England.
questions.explanation: Name of the game 'Darts' takes singular 'is'.

questions.question: The United Nations ______ founded in 1945.
questions.explanation: Names of organizations take a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Twenty kilograms of rice ______ enough for our family.
questions.explanation: Quantities expressing a single weight or measure take singular 'is'.

questions.question: Five years ______ a long time to wait.
questions.explanation: Periods of time treated as a single duration take singular 'is'.

questions.question: The staff ______ unhappy with the new decision.
questions.explanation: Collective noun referring to employees as individuals takes plural 'are'.

questions.question: A group of tourists ______ visiting the palace.
questions.explanation: 'A group of' takes a singular verb focusing on the single unit ('is').

questions.question: A fleet of ships ______ sailing in the harbor.
questions.explanation: 'A fleet of' is a singular collective noun, taking 'is'.

questions.question: A pack of wolves ______ spotted in the forest.
questions.explanation: 'A pack of' takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: The luggage ______ heavy.
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable and takes singular 'is'.

questions.question: His advice ______ always helpful.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun taking singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: The furniture in our house ______ made of teak.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun taking singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Information ______ power.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, taking singular 'is'.

questions.question: The majority of students ______ passed the examination.
questions.explanation: 'The majority of' + countable plural noun takes a plural verb ('have').

questions.question: A number of soldiers ______ injured in the combat.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' is followed by a plural verb ('were').

questions.question: The number of road accidents ______ decreasing this year.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' denotes a singular statistical count and takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Not only Rahul but also his friends ______ coming to the party.
questions.explanation: With 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('friends' -> 'are').

questions.question: Neither the teacher nor the principal ______ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: Both subjects joined by 'neither... nor' are singular, taking singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Neither the students nor the teacher ______ happy with the results.
questions.explanation: Verb agrees with the closer subject ('teacher' -> 'was').

questions.question: Either Mohan or his brothers ______ to be blamed.
questions.explanation: Verb agrees with closer plural subject ('brothers' -> 'are').

questions.question: Fifty thousand rupees ______ paid to the contractor yesterday.
questions.explanation: When money is disbursed in individual transactions/payments, it can take plural verb ('were paid').

questions.question: Five thousand rupees ______ a large amount fifty years ago.
questions.explanation: Considered as a single lump-sum figure, it takes a singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Mathematics ______ an interesting subject.
questions.explanation: Subject name ending in '-s' takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: His mathematics ______ very weak.
questions.explanation: When 'mathematics' refers to calculation abilities of a person, it takes plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Politics ______ a dirty game.
questions.explanation: Name of discipline/field takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: His politics ______ conservative.
questions.explanation: When 'politics' refers to personal political beliefs, it takes plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Economics ______ taught by Professor Sharma.
questions.explanation: Academic discipline takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: The acoustics of this auditorium ______ excellent.
questions.explanation: 'Acoustics' referring to physical sound properties takes plural verb ('are').

questions.question: Measles ______ a contagious viral disease.
questions.explanation: Name of a disease ending in '-s' takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Mumps ______ common among children.
questions.explanation: Name of disease takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Rickets ______ caused by vitamin D deficiency.

questions.question: Six months ______ a long period to wait.
questions.explanation: Time interval considered as a whole takes singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Three-fourths of the wall ______ completed.
questions.explanation: Fraction of a singular object takes singular verb ('was').

questions.question: Two-thirds of the students ______ absent.
